pcp-short-abstract.PCP.np_subset_pcp: The verifier, machine implementation and constants are chosen once for the language. The polynomial in `ReadsBelow` bounds the largest possible proof address even when later queries depend on earlier answers, which lets the converse use a finite witness.

pcp-short-forward-statement.PCP.np_subset_pcp: `CanonicalRandomness` fixes the exact seed length $\alpha\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+\beta$. The bound applies to the machine that produces the query tree, and the separate `ReadsBelow` clause bounds all the addresses the tree can reach.
pcp-short-forward-statement.PCP.ReferenceNP.inNP_iff_mem: The forward theorem takes `PCP.InNP Machine.PolyTimeRel` as its hypothesis. To apply it to a language in the reference nondeterministic-machine class, use the right-to-left direction of `inNP_iff_mem` to obtain a concrete witness checker.

pcp-short-theorem.PCP.np_subset_pcp: Suppose the verifier has two seeds. A proof that passes only the first and another that passes only the second each have acceptance probability $1/2$. Perfect completeness requires one proof that passes both. This is why a deterministic checker can use one candidate proof prefix and enumerate the seeds in the converse.

pcp-short-colour-constraints.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorGrid.colorable_i: The existential direction starts with a three-colouring and interpolates its grid values to obtain the degree bound. The reverse direction restricts a witness polynomial to the grid and uses the primitive cube root to identify the solutions of $u^3=1$ with the three colours.
pcp-short-colour-constraints.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorGrid.constraints: Take two vertices labelled with the same allowed colour. Their difference is zero, so the edge expression is $E(X,Y)(-1)$. It is nonzero on an edge and zero on a nonedge. This is why one interpolated adjacency table $E$ can enforce the proper-colouring condition over the whole pair grid, where $E$ takes only the values zero and one.
pcp-short-colour-constraints.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorGrid.totalDegree: The cube can triple the total degree, while subtracting the constant one cannot increase that bound. The same degree ceiling will apply to a vanishing certificate for the vertex constraint.

The adjacency table is interpolated in the coordinates of both vertices. Each coordinate contributes at most $h-1$ to total degree, so the graph contributes $2d_0$ to the $5d_0$ bound for the edge constraint.

Multiplying by $E$ restricts the colouring equation to edges on the grid and costs $\deg E$ in the degree budget. With $\deg Q\le d_0$ and $\deg E\le 2d_0$, cubing $Q$ and multiplying gives the $5d_0$ ceiling.

pcp-short-vanishing-certificate.PCP.Algebraic.GridVanishing.vanishesOn_i: For $H=\{0,1\}$, take $A(X_1,X_2)=(X_1^2-X_1)X_2+(X_2^2-X_2)$. Replace the two vanishing factors by new variables to get $M(X,Y)=Y_1X_2+Y_2$. Substituting $Y=0$ gives zero, and substituting $Y=Z_H(X)$ gives $A$. The verifier checks these two identities on encoded evaluations instead of querying one quotient for each grid coordinate.

pcp-short-digit-evaluation.PCP.Algebraic.SetMultilinear.eval_encode: With base three and two positions, $5=2+1\cdot3$, so $Y^5$ becomes $X_{0,2}X_{1,1}$. At $\Phi(z)$ this is $z^2z^3=z^5$. The degree-nine cutoff keeps every exponent within the two available positions. This lets the honest prover store a high-degree line restriction in a form whose total degree is only two in this example.

pcp-short-proof-table-type.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.Proof: The `Proof` fields are functions returning bits at typed addresses. There is no consistency premise between a points table and its lines table, so the soundness theorem can start with arbitrary received answers.

pcp-short-query-type.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.Query: Each constructor selects a table and fixes the type of label a query can use. A lines-table query also takes the base and slope of an outer line and an inner evaluation point, so it addresses one bit of the encoded restriction.
pcp-short-query-type.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.read: `read` dispatches to the selected field of `Proof` and returns one bit. When the proof is honest, the value arises from the construction of the table being read, with the same read operation used for arbitrary proofs.

pcp-short-honest-value.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.honestP: A points-table address asks for a bit of a polynomial's value at one field point. A lines-table address first selects a line, which fixes a univariate restriction, then asks for a bit of that restriction's digit encoding at an inner evaluation point. These two ways of storing related information are what the low-degree test compares at a sampled point of the line.

pcp-short-weighted-test.PCP.Algebraic.GeneratorLowDegreeTest.exi: For a polynomial linear along a line, two values at distinct nonzero parameters determine its value at parameter zero. The tester compares that prediction with the stored value. The theorem extends the rule to $c+1$ generator nodes and turns a high rate of passing random checks into one nearby polynomial of total degree at most $c$. The strict error threshold and $q>2c$ enter that second implication.

pcp-short-binary-decoding.PCP.Algebraic.BinaryLocalRowDecoding.exi: In three binary coordinates at label degree three, there are $256$ full labels and just $8$ homogeneous linear labels. Changing every homogeneous entry can therefore give full-label error $1/32$ while the homogeneous error relative to the same word is one. The two conclusions for one polynomial $U$ let the verifier use the full distribution for masked reads and the homogeneous distribution for its linear comparisons.

pcp-short-point-line.PCP.Algebraic.PointLineTest.exists_close: A geometric line with two parameterizations can be supplied twice with incompatible polynomials. Even so, each comparison uses the same points table at the selected point. If disagreement is sufficiently rare under the stated field-size bound, the theorem recovers one global polynomial from these independent line entries. The binary test applies it after converting label disagreements into field disagreements.

pcp-short-outer-decoding.PCP.Algebraic.EncodedLineLowDegreeTest.e: The bound on $J\kappa$ puts the decoded point-versus-line data in the small-error range. The conclusion estimates two distances to the same polynomial of degree at most $cb^c$, giving both the full-label control used in composed reads and the homogeneous control used in linear checks.

pcp-short-outer-correction.PCP.Algebraic.BinaryLocalCorrection.fail: Start with Madhu Sudan’s Probabilistically Checkable Proofs, Lecture 2, §4, and reconstruct a degree-$d$ field value at a fixed target from $d+1$ distinct nonzero line parameters. Check why each sampled position is uniform on its own, then justify the union bound even though the positions share a slope. The binary corrector here has an extra job because its line table is also received from the prover. A table on $F^2$ can be wrong on the entire row $y=0$ with average error only $1/q$. To recover a bit at a prescribed target $a$, compare the proposed line value at $a+zv$, which is uniform when $v$ is uniform and $z\ne0$. A line polynomial wrong at $a$ can match the correct line at at most $D$ of its $q-1$ nonzero parameters. The bound includes both an incorrect returned bit and rejection, with $\kappa_a$ measured at this target.

pcp-short-zero.PCP.Algebraic.BinaryZeroOnGridCorrection: If $A$ is nonzero somewhere on the grid, the two certificate identities cannot both be polynomial identities. Schwartz–Zippel and a random homogeneous label give the left-hand bound. The two certificate reads account for the factor two on $\delta_M$ and the two contributions to the correction cost.

pcp-short-derived-zero.PCP.Algebraic.DerivedZeroOnGrid.rejectio: The composed label need not be uniform, so the verifier reads at a uniform mask and at its translate by the composed label. Each read contributes at most $\epsilon$ of full-label error. The degree bound $r$ ensures that the composed label is in the table.

linked-source-12.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.exists_: With one grid coordinate and two grid elements, the worst degree bound $5m(h-1)$ is five. Base two and three digit positions then suffice since $5<8$. In general the same comparison must hold for the largest degree bound, including that of the edge certificate, to make every honest line evaluation exact. This is what lets a single proof from a colouring pass on every seed.
linked-source-12.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorVerifier.test_ho: With the certificate identities supplied directly, every honest read satisfies the check it enters. The strict degree premises allow exact recovery of each honest line restriction under the encoding substitution. The theorem takes a seed as an arbitrary argument, so the same proof works for all seeds.

linked-source-13.PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColorAmplifiedVerifie: These are the guarantees after fair-bit sampling and repetition. `verification_guarantees` records the chosen positive $R$, the query and seed budgets multiplied by $R$, and the final error $1/2$. The single-run rejection gap appears earlier in the proof.

pcp-short-complexity.PCP.Lang.ThreeColorRuntime.polyTimeAlg: `polyTimeAlg` bounds the running time of the amplified algorithm in the concrete machine model. The field and root searches contribute through the imported construction, so the assertion covers the computation needed to produce queries as well as the queries themselves.

linked-source-14.PCP.pcp_subset_np_concrete: The address bound lets the NP witness contain just $p(n)$ bits. A concrete checker enumerates the polynomially many seeds and accepts if every run accepts. Perfect completeness supplies a passing witness, while soundness ensures that any candidate on a no-input fails at least one seed.

pcp-short-reference-np.PCP.ReferenceNP.inNP_iff_mem: The equivalence transports the two PCP implications to the reference definition of NP. The machine-to-checker direction supplies the forward theorem’s hypothesis, and the checker-to-machine direction converts the converse’s output to reference NP membership.
